properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/04/2021 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Clarion Twp, Clarion county. 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery.  Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/04/2021
Violation Code: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 932395
Permit API: 031-23576
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Clarion Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/04/2021
Comments: This is a well located within 2500' of an active gas migration area. At the time of inspection, well was equipped to produce. The tubing valve was closed, but the 4 1/2" was tied in and the valve pinched open. The annulus was closed. The well integrity appeared good at surface and no leaks were detected. However, I picked up as high as 46% LEL in the ground outside of the wellhead, farthest from the tank and then 8% gas between the wellhead and tank. Due to this, there is a problem with the well integrity downhole and the well is in violation. The well was labeled and equipped with a check calve, separator, line heater, regulator, and chart (last changed on 9/13). There was also a 100 bbl fiberglass tank tied in. The compressor had been shut off on September 28th, as you can see on the Barton chart where there is a pressure increase.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to SWN PROD CO LLC in Liberty Twp, Tioga County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 08/26/2020 to SWN PROD CO LLC in Liberty Twp, Tioga county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 08/26/2020
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 892776
Permit API: 117-22026
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 08/26/2020
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report from the operator that 15 gallons of produced water was spilled to the pad surface on August 25, 2019. I was accompanied during this inspection by DEP EP Specialist Justin Abbott and Mike Deming of SWN. According to Mr. Deming, a truck was offloading produced water from a frac tank battery when both the pop off valve on the truck released and the hose failed, releasing produced water to the pad surface. Based on the volume of in the truck, the volume of the spill is estimated at 15 gallons. A puddle of stormwater was present adjacent to the area where the spill occurred. SWN determined that this puddle had been impacted by the release so the puddle was removed and this area of the pad was also excavated. Mr. Deming said that a total of 30 tons of material was excavated. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/08/2025 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Asylum Township, Bradford county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/05/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8251316
Permit API: 015-23861
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/08/2025
Comments: On 10/08/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand) Kerrick Unit OG Well Pad in Asylum Township, Bradford County. The weather was 56 degrees and partly sunny. I arrived at 1025 hours. The site appears stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There was an infiltration berm onsite. It appeared to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 190.6 us/cm- 4.15 mS/cm (photo #4 and 5). Soil was field measured for EC at ~4.00 mS/cm (photo #6). Pooled water in area of the reported release on 06/04/2025 (IR #3990710 and CTS #389602) was field measured for EC between 2.04-4.15 mS/cm. The elevated pooled water was observed behind the produced fluid tank.The DEP spoke with Expand representative Mike Deming via phone and he stated their consultants visited the site the same day and confirmed the elevated water around the produced fluid tank. The release was then reported to the DEP via the 24 hour number. Expand will begin remediation on 10/09/2025. The quantity of the release is unknown. The following reoccurring violations are cited against API #015-23861:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)Due to the unknown quantity of the release this will be referred to Act 2 for compliance. The following violations remain open against API #015-23861:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)This case has been referred to the Environmental cleanups and Brownfields program and all violations will remain outstanding until results have been reviewed and compared to Act 2 standards by the ECB program, and an approval letter has been issued.I departed at 1125 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/22/2025 to DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/22/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8242720
Permit API: 129-26521
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/22/2025
Comments: On July 22, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3985188 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3985188, remedial excavation was completed and the impacted soil was stockpiled onsite awaiting disposal. The impacted soil stockpiles were covered and appeared to be adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 2). However, leaking gas was audible from the top of the well head (see photo 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The brine tank that was present at the time of the Department's previous surface inspection has been replaced. The newly-installed brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no elevated soil conductivity detected underneath the brine tank valve (see photos 7-9 and 18). It appears that the stained material noted underneath the brine tank during the time of IR 3967072 has been removed (see photo 10). It appears that the impacted soil stockpiles have been removed from site, as they were not present onsite during this inspection.The slope that was impacted by the 4/24/2025 release has been backfilled, mulched, and seeded. It has established some vegetative coverage, although it is inconsistent at the time of inspection (see photos 11, 13, and 14). An erosion rill has developed at the top of this slope (see photo 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) and straw bales are installed at the bottom of the formerly impacted slope (see photo 15). No elevated soil conductivity was detected in this location or at the approximate downslope edge of the formerly impacted area (see photos 16-18).The Department notified the operator of the erosion rill observed during this inspection via voicemail, and recommended that it is repaired and measures are taken to protect it from heavy stormwater events while it establishes vegetative coverage.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remedial work has been completed and the site awaits completion of re-stabilization. However, violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding, as an NOI to Remediate and/or Final Report has not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB for review.Additional violations may be forthcoming pending reassessment and reevaluation of the erosion rill in a future follow-up inspection conducted by the Department.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/26/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Georges Township, Fayette county. 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/26/2026
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8275980
Permit API: 051-23703
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Georges Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/26/2026
Comments: On 5/26/2026, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection at the Jobes 1 well plugging site in Georges Township, Fayette County. Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart (Next Level Energy) was on site conducting plugging operations during this inspection.The Department issued an Order to Diversified (#445705) on August 15, 2025. According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance. However, the RCE is partially laden with sediment at the time of inspection. Additional sediment was observed in the neighboring residential yard and on Jobes Drive. The sediment observed on Jobes Drive appeared to be tracked approximately 150 feet from the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE). Significant tire rutting was observed in the neighboring residential yard and in the access road. The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan is available on site.Upon arriving to the well plugging site, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart. Lockhart cautioned the Department that high-pressure lines are active around the gas well, and suggested against approaching the plugging rig during this inspection. Therefore, the area surrounding the well plugging rig was not evaluated during this inspection due to the hazards present.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to maintain the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE), the tire rutting in the access road, the sediment tracked onto Jobes Drive, and for conducting plugging operations in a manner that causes a public nuisance.

Comments: On 5/26/2026, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection at the Jobes 1 well plugging site in Georges Township, Fayette County. Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart (Next Level Energy) was on site conducting plugging operations during this inspection.The Department issued an Order to Diversified (#445705) on August 15, 2025. According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance. However, the RCE is partially laden with sediment at the time of inspection. Additional sediment was observed in the neighboring residential yard and on Jobes Drive. The sediment observed on Jobes Drive appeared to be tracked approximately 150 feet from the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE). Significant tire rutting was observed in the neighboring residential yard and in the access road. The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan is available on site.Upon arriving to the well plugging site, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart. Lockhart cautioned the Department that high-pressure lines are active around the gas well, and suggested against approaching the plugging rig during this inspection. Therefore, the area surrounding the well plugging rig was not evaluated during this inspection due to the hazards present.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to maintain the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE), the tire rutting in the access road, the sediment tracked onto Jobes Drive, and for conducting plugging operations in a manner that causes a public nuisance.

Unconventional: No

Comments: On 8/19/25 at 12:55 p.m. OGI John Shaffer conducted a follow up onsite inspection of Rush 3 OG WELL permit number 051-23512. This is a 90 day follow up. At the time of inspection, the well and the production unit appear to be inline and producing. Production annulus is connected to production, and the valves appear open. Vent on intermediate annulus has been removed, and is now connected to a small tank. No spills were observed or detected at the well, or separator. Operator posting is present and attached to the chart box. The Annual Production Report indicates 652 thousand cubic feet of gas for 2024. The Mechanical Integrity Assessments show 125 pounds per square inch, "N" in the corrosion problems column and, "surface corrosion may be present" in the comments for production year 2024. Venting from the intermediate casing with the fiber wrap was previously detected and verified with MSA Altair 5X Multi Gas Detector. The intermediate annulus is now connected to a tank and gas can be visually observed coming from around the cap and out of the small hole in top of cap. Gas was verified at base of tank cap with MSA Altair 5X. Readings indicated 100% methane and 509 parts per million on CO. Violations are being continued at this time.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to K PETROLEUM INC in Somerset Township, Washington County
properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 8/19/2026 to K PETROLEUM INC in Somerset Township, Washington county. 78a55(i)4ii - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Sign - Failure of the operator to meet requirements of site entrance sign fabrication, color, size, lettering, wording, numbering, format, information and location.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: K PETROLEUM INC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 8/19/2026
Violation Code: 78a55(i)4ii - EMERGNCY RESPONSE – Sign - Failure of the operator to meet requirements of site entrance sign fabrication, color, size, lettering, wording, numbering, format, information and location.
Violation ID: 8286047
Permit API: 125-23924
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2026
Comments: On August 19, 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the Cecil 2-P229 OG Well in regard to CTS 400392.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.At the time of the inspection the well was located in an open agricultural field. The access road appeared stabilized. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting were present onsite appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.There appeared to be 3 total production tanks onsite. Upon further inspection, it appeared the white poly tank was connected and in use. The tank appeared to be in sound condition with no observed leaks or discharges of fluid were observed around this tank.Two metal tanks were also present onsite but did not appear to be in use at the time of the inspection. Upon further inspection of the 2 metal tanks, one of the tanks appeared to be severely corroded with multiple holes in the tank observed. The Department observed fluid flowing down the side of the tank. A conductivity reading of this fluid was obtained and was "OR" (Over detectable range, >20mS). Upon inspection of the ground surrounding the corroded production tank, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of staining and saturation with readings of 12.78mS, 9.24mS, 4.37mS, and 1.82mS being obtained. These readings are elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.19mS. Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings, it appears a release has/is occurring from the corroded production tank.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's observations of an apparent release. Mr. Inghram stated the metal tanks have been disconnected and empty for several years. The Department recommended remediation of the spill and removal of the production tanks as they are no longer in use and heavily corroded. Mr. Inghram stated he would get a contractor to begin the work as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/18/2025 to OIL & GAS MGMT INC in Parks Township, Armstrong county. 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/18/2025
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8249194
Permit API: 005-29119
Unconventional: No
County: Armstrong
Municipality: Parks Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: On Thursday, 9/18/2025, I conducted an inspection of the Oil and Gas Management, Inc. Brown 2 well, permit number 005-29119, due to complaint received 9/16/2025 (CTS #392326). The site is located in the woods off of Chestnut Road in Parks township, Armstrong county. The complaint was submitted as a result of a spill on the site. The spill appears to be used motor oil and I estimated that more than 25 gallons was spilled. This was due to containers (2 - 5 gallon buckets and a 55 gallon drum) and refuse (used oil filter) observed in the immediate area of the spill (see pictures 3, 4, and 5). The operator did not report the spill and it appears that the operator has not visited the site recently. The well was shut in on the day of the inspection, but the operator did report a non-averaged production of 729.0 mcf for the 2024 production (365 days producing, as per OGRE). The well appeared to be disconnected from the compressor (see picture 9) and the compressor does not appear to be functional at this time (no motor, see picture 8). It needs to be noted that the production chart is dated 4-2-23 (see picture 3). The site access road is also in terrible condition. The E and S BMP's have not been maintained and there are multiple areas that are deeply rutted and have significant accelerated erosion.As a result of the site conditions, the operator is being cited for violations to 25 PA Code 78.53, 102.22(a), 102.4(b)(1), 78.57(a), 78.66(b), and CSL 402(b)

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/20/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/20/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8245734
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/20/2025
Comments: On August 20, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4022927 and violations issued for a 1 barrel release of a production/reuse water.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that had a different Operator's information posted on it. The Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues.At the time of this inspection, the gravel in the previous area of the release appeared to have been scraped/excavated. According to the operator's NOV response, remediation (via excavation) of impacted materials was completed on July 30 2025. There appeared to be rain water puddles in the area of the previous release and scraping of the contaminated gravel. The Department did not observe a sheen in any puddles of apparent rainwater in the release area. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the release area and collected the following soil conductivity readings: 0.32mS, 0.77mS, 0.48mS. These readings were found to be comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.67 mS.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at thus time pending the Act 2 Final report submittal, receipt, review, and approval by the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfield Program

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8202435
Permit API: 129-25561
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/19/2024
Comments: On September 19, 2024, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Mountain View's George A Willlaims 4 well located in South Huntington Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3726379 where violations were issued for a spill from the production tank. A Notice of Violation response was received by the Department on May 16, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road which is off of a residential home's driveway appears stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the well site is located in a field adjacent to the residence home. The production tank that was leaking during IR 3726379 appears to be removed from the well site and the area where it sat appears to be the only area of the well site that is lacking 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. A well tag is fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the well head. Production equipment on site appears to be heavily rusted, the Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the production equipment to ensure corrosion does not worsen and compromise the structural integrity.A background soil conductivity reading was taken in some vegetation up slope of the well site (0.1781 mS) and then several soil conductivity readings were taken in the area where the production tank once sat (0.562 mS, 0.718 mS, 0.1278 mS, 0.229 mS, 0.582 mS, 0.539 mS, 0.1788 mS, 0.619 mS, and 0.1467 mS). Some of the conductivity readings are elevated compared to the background reading while some readings in the same soil type are not elevated and are comparable to the background reading, subjugating that the issue is not the type of soil in this area, but that some of the contaminated soil has not yet been removed from the well site.The Department is recommending the Operator remove the remaining contaminated soil, dispose of it properly and replace it with fresh topsoil as well as seed and mulch to bring the entire site up to 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Based on today's inspection, violations issue during IR 3726379 shall remain outstanding at this time.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/08/2024 to PENNECO OIL CO INC in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNECO OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/08/2024
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8182725
Permit API: 129-28783
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/08/2024
Comments: On April 8, 2024, inspection conducted on the Tutelo 2 well in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred the day prior to this inspection at 7:00 PM, and was reported to the Department that same evening at approximately 9:00 PM by Penneco representative Marc Jacobs (see attached Spill Report). The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Jacobs while en route to the well site, who explained that a dry-rotted high-pressure hose connected to the well ruptured and released from 1 to 2 barrels of oil onsite. He subsequently explained that Penneco representatives were working nearby when they heard the hose rupture and were able to initiate a prompt response. Present with the Department during this inspection were Woodard and Curran consultants Matt Kapral and Clayton Hefner. Additional representatives from Penneco and Woodard and Curran were also onsite.This inspection report is part 1 of 2, covering the Department's inspection in response to this incident.The following was observed:The access road to the well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). This access road is shared with the Tutelo 1 (129-23915) well site. Materials were staged along the access road for installation of CFS (see photo 2). An unnamed stream or tributary was observed approximately 150 feet south of the well site that flows through a culvert underneath the access road. An oil absorbent boom was observed in this location (see photo 3). The Department spoke with Mr. Kapral and Mr. Hefner who explained that seven additional oil absorbent booms were placed across the unnamed stream or tributary downslope of the cross-culvert under the access road. They further explained that a sheen was observed where the first oil absorbent boom was placed upstream from the access road culvert. Peatmoss was spread on impacted areas not yet excavated onsite (see photos 5 and 6). Brush clearing was conducted on the slope east of the well site to remove impacted vegetation and prepare for excavation of impacted soil (see photos 7 and 8). Minor excavation work had been conducted upon arrival to site to contain impacted material, according to onsite representatives (see photos 9 and 18). Additional excavations were conducted while the Department was onsite. Onsite brine tanks appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 10). A large tarp was laid west of well site for placement of excavated impacted material (see photo 11). Heavy oil staining was observed on the ground around the well head upon arrival to site (see photo 14). It was equipped with a well tag, and the operator's information was posted on the separator (see photos 16 and 17). The aforementioned sheen was observed upstream of the access road culvert, with fluid beading on the wet rocks in this location (see photos 19 and 20). Due to observations made in this location, the Department subsequently collected water samples in this location. While the Department sampled, CFS installations were conducted (see photos 21 and 22). The overall size of the impacted ground area appeared to be approximately 100 feet by 100 feet at the well site, with approximately 100 additional feet of the access road also being impacted. An oil odor was detectable within an approximate 150 foot radius of the well site. Based on observations from this inspection, remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2 is recommended. Violations are being issued in response to observations made during this inspection. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt of analytical results from samples collected during this inspection. Please see IR 3742855 for inspection report documenting the Department's collection of aqueous samples from the onsite unnamed stream or tributary.

Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNECO OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/08/2024
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8182725
Permit API: 129-28783
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/08/2024
Comments: On April 8, 2024, inspection conducted on the Tutelo 2 well in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred the day prior to this inspection at 7:00 PM, and was reported to the Department that same evening at approximately 9:00 PM by Penneco representative Marc Jacobs (see attached Spill Report). The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Jacobs while en route to the well site, who explained that a dry-rotted high-pressure hose connected to the well ruptured and released from 1 to 2 barrels of oil onsite. He subsequently explained that Penneco representatives were working nearby when they heard the hose rupture and were able to initiate a prompt response. Present with the Department during this inspection were Woodard and Curran consultants Matt Kapral and Clayton Hefner. Additional representatives from Penneco and Woodard and Curran were also onsite.This inspection report is part 1 of 2, covering the Department's inspection in response to this incident.The following was observed:The access road to the well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). This access road is shared with the Tutelo 1 (129-23915) well site. Materials were staged along the access road for installation of CFS (see photo 2). An unnamed stream or tributary was observed approximately 150 feet south of the well site that flows through a culvert underneath the access road. An oil absorbent boom was observed in this location (see photo 3). The Department spoke with Mr. Kapral and Mr. Hefner who explained that seven additional oil absorbent booms were placed across the unnamed stream or tributary downslope of the cross-culvert under the access road. They further explained that a sheen was observed where the first oil absorbent boom was placed upstream from the access road culvert. Peatmoss was spread on impacted areas not yet excavated onsite (see photos 5 and 6). Brush clearing was conducted on the slope east of the well site to remove impacted vegetation and prepare for excavation of impacted soil (see photos 7 and 8). Minor excavation work had been conducted upon arrival to site to contain impacted material, according to onsite representatives (see photos 9 and 18). Additional excavations were conducted while the Department was onsite. Onsite brine tanks appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 10). A large tarp was laid west of well site for placement of excavated impacted material (see photo 11). Heavy oil staining was observed on the ground around the well head upon arrival to site (see photo 14). It was equipped with a well tag, and the operator's information was posted on the separator (see photos 16 and 17). The aforementioned sheen was observed upstream of the access road culvert, with fluid beading on the wet rocks in this location (see photos 19 and 20). Due to observations made in this location, the Department subsequently collected water samples in this location. While the Department sampled, CFS installations were conducted (see photos 21 and 22). The overall size of the impacted ground area appeared to be approximately 100 feet by 100 feet at the well site, with approximately 100 additional feet of the access road also being impacted. An oil odor was detectable within an approximate 150 foot radius of the well site. Based on observations from this inspection, remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2 is recommended. Violations are being issued in response to observations made during this inspection. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt of analytical results from samples collected during this inspection. Please see IR 3742855 for inspection report documenting the Department's collection of aqueous samples from the onsite unnamed stream or tributary.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/11/2023 to STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC in Howe Twp, Forest county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 995095
Permit API: 053-29816
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack that appears to have been recently produced. A sticker is posted on the pump jack displaying the operator's information, the well's API number is written on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. An approximate 2' x 5' area of vegetation and soil are stained with a coating of crude oil on the well site from the apparent repeated venting of this well into the atmosphere. The same practice is prevalent at a majority of the well sites on the Warrant 2980 lease and will be addressed in a separate inspection report. A tank battery that is located approximately 250' southeast of well consists of four steel and six plastic storage tanks inside of an earthen diking. There are several areas of stained gravel near the tanks (and at a compressor that is also located inside of the diking) which is indicative of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the containment.The exterior (southern) wall of the diking is void of vegetation and the specific conductance (SPC) is elevated (3800 uS/cm per field meter). It appears that the production fluid that has been released into the gravel inside of the tank battery diking has migrated through the southern wall of the containment and into a roadside ditch that flows south towards a cross culvert approximately 200 feet south of the well. Stressed vegetation, elevated SPC readings and abundant deer tracks are present in the ditch between the tank battery and the cross culvert and continue in a channel down to the next lease road (near 053-29533) approximately 300 feet beyond the culvert outlet.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29907, 053-29935 and 053-29916 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. Additional E and S concerns on this lease are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29536 (Warrant 2980 #37).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/03/2025 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Sheffield Township, Warren county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/03/2025
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8254675
Permit API: 123-49141
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sheffield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/03/2025
Comments: This recently drilled conventional well was shut in. Drill cuttings have been directed into a lined pit. The drilling permit and E and S Plan were posted at the entrance of the location. The access road and well site location have been stoned, however, due to the recent drilling traffic during wet conditions the road material has lost its durability. The road leading to the well was reshaped after the rig moved out, however, clean stone should be considered to provide a durable road surface for the upcoming completion and production of this well. Due to the lack of energy dissipators and culverts, the road ditch is experiencing high flow, and is therefore, showing signs of accelerated erosion. The ditch will need to be reshaped, graded, and temporarily stabilized. Additional culverts, as called for in the E and S Plan, will need to be installed in order for the ditch to function properly. Only 2 out of the 4 culverts called for in the E and S Plan have been installed. The 2 culverts installed have not been installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. The lone culvert on the slope of the access road leading to the well site is poorly positioned with a majority of stormwater flow bypassing the inlet and continuing to flow down the ditch rather than out-letting through the culvert. According to the E and S Plan, stone rip-rap should be placed below the outlets to dissipate the outfall. Infiltration berms should be installed beyond the outlet of the culverts. The outlets are directing stormwater at un-stabilized fill material from the construction of the road. None of the outlets have stone rip-rap or an infiltration berm to dissipate the outfall of stormwater. These concerns should be addressed as outlined in the E and S Plan.A majority of the seed and mulch on the road banks and surrounding the well location have washed away with only sparse vegetation established. These areas will need to be re-seeded and mulched in order to eventually achieve permanent stabilization, prevent accelerated erosion from occurring, and meet the requirements of Chapter 102. The recent drilling traffic has also caused significant rutting on FR 413A. This road is expected to be properly shaped with a functional ditch or other measures to manage stormwater. Clean stone should be considered in certain areas to improve the durability given the additional development related traffic that will be using this road. Also, installing tail ditches or other measures to improve the drainage of the road should be considered to allow for the road to remain in compliance throughout the remaining development of this well and well #1. A follow up inspection will be conducted to ensure the above concerns have been addressed properly and in a timely manner. Due to the risk of pollution via accelerated erosion and sedimentation it is highly recommended to address these concerns prior to the next rain event.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/11/2022 to PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC in Keating Twp, Potter county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 955461
Permit API: 105-21845
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/11/2022
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the PGE – Hancock Pad A located in Keating Twp, Potter Co. on 5/12/22 @1210 hours in response to a reported release of approximately 10 barrels of brine to the pad surface (CID#364034). The weather was 73 degrees, sunny, winds ENE@3mph. Mr. Chad Earley, PGE HSE Supervisor and Mr. Matt Covine, PGE Completions Consultant were present onsite for the inspection. Mr. Earley stated a cement truck was parked in secondary containment yesterday during the previous days plugging activities. A brine solution was spilled into the secondary containment from the truck. At the end of yesteday’s plugging activities, the secondary containment was "almost full" of the brine solution. The brine solution was left in the secondary containment overnight. Mr. Earley stated when Mr. Covine arrived onsite the next morning, there was less brine solution in the secondary containment and visible staining and fluid on the pad surface. Mr. Earley estimates 10 barrels of fluid was released to the pad surface. I screened the fluid remaining in the secondary containment with an Oakton Multiparameter meter. The field conductivity was measured at 18.8mS/cm. Damp areas around the secondary containment were screened with a Groline soil conductivity meter and found to be >4.0mS/cm. Two vac trucks arrived onsite to remove the fluid remaining in the secondary containment as well as the brine solution remaining in the two water tanks adjacent to the spill area. The secondary containment responsible for the release was lifted with a telehandler and the underside examined. The Secondary containment appeared to have a seam that was not properly sealed, this allowed fluid to leak from the bottom of the containment. The visibly impacted area was estimated to cover ~20’ long x 12’ wide. As material was excavated and placed into a lined rolloff waste container, a clay layer was encountered approximately 14" below the pad surface. Mr. Earley screened the clay material with a field conductivity meter and found the material measured <500uS/cm. Mr. Earley stated the clay later appeared to be a barrier for further infiltration of the brine solution. Mr. Earley also stated the brine solution appeared to have laterally migrated under the brine tank containment adjacent to the excavated spill area. Mr. Earley stated their plan was to excavate the 12’ x 20’ impacted area, while field screening, to ensure all impacted areas are identified. PGE would then line the area with plastic and backfill with clean gravel to accommodate completion of the plugging activity. Mr. Earley stated PGE would then have the tanks and their containment removed to further screen the area under the tanks and remove any additional impacted material. I requested Mr. Earley email me pictures of today's completed cleanup activities and provided my contact information. Due to the reported volume of the release being greater than 42 gallons the operator must demonstrate attainment of one or more of the standards established by Act 2 and Chapter 250. This incident is referred to the DEP Cleanups Program for Follow-up. Violations of the following regulations are cited against the Hancock Pad A 2741 Well (API#105-21845) at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a.64(b) 25 Pa Code 78a.64(f) CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 I departed the site at 1440 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the PGE – Hancock Pad A located in Keating Twp, Potter Co. on 5/12/22 @1210 hours in response to a reported release of approximately 10 barrels of brine to the pad surface (CID#364034). The weather was 73 degrees, sunny, winds ENE@3mph. Mr. Chad Earley, PGE HSE Supervisor and Mr. Matt Covine, PGE Completions Consultant were present onsite for the inspection. Mr. Earley stated a cement truck was parked in secondary containment yesterday during the previous days plugging activities. A brine solution was spilled into the secondary containment from the truck. At the end of yesteday’s plugging activities, the secondary containment was "almost full" of the brine solution. The brine solution was left in the secondary containment overnight. Mr. Earley stated when Mr. Covine arrived onsite the next morning, there was less brine solution in the secondary containment and visible staining and fluid on the pad surface. Mr. Earley estimates 10 barrels of fluid was released to the pad surface. I screened the fluid remaining in the secondary containment with an Oakton Multiparameter meter. The field conductivity was measured at 18.8mS/cm. Damp areas around the secondary containment were screened with a Groline soil conductivity meter and found to be >4.0mS/cm. Two vac trucks arrived onsite to remove the fluid remaining in the secondary containment as well as the brine solution remaining in the two water tanks adjacent to the spill area. The secondary containment responsible for the release was lifted with a telehandler and the underside examined. The Secondary containment appeared to have a seam that was not properly sealed, this allowed fluid to leak from the bottom of the containment. The visibly impacted area was estimated to cover ~20’ long x 12’ wide. As material was excavated and placed into a lined rolloff waste container, a clay layer was encountered approximately 14" below the pad surface. Mr. Earley screened the clay material with a field conductivity meter and found the material measured <500uS/cm. Mr. Earley stated the clay later appeared to be a barrier for further infiltration of the brine solution. Mr. Earley also stated the brine solution appeared to have laterally migrated under the brine tank containment adjacent to the excavated spill area. Mr. Earley stated their plan was to excavate the 12’ x 20’ impacted area, while field screening, to ensure all impacted areas are identified. PGE would then line the area with plastic and backfill with clean gravel to accommodate completion of the plugging activity. Mr. Earley stated PGE would then have the tanks and their containment removed to further screen the area under the tanks and remove any additional impacted material. I requested Mr. Earley email me pictures of today's completed cleanup activities and provided my contact information. Due to the reported volume of the release being greater than 42 gallons the operator must demonstrate attainment of one or more of the standards established by Act 2 and Chapter 250. This incident is referred to the DEP Cleanups Program for Follow-up. Violations of the following regulations are cited against the Hancock Pad A 2741 Well (API#105-21845) at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a.64(b) 25 Pa Code 78a.64(f) CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 I departed the site at 1440 hours.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build-Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on both wells on the DeWolf pad, the Evelyn Wyo. 4H and the Evelyn Wyo. 2H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess recent remedial work of Perf. and Squeeze Ops. The Evelyn Wyo. 4H wells Conductor x Surface (20"x 13 3/8") annulus has an open casing top in cellar, the Evelyn Wyo. 2H Conductor by Surface (20" x13 3/8") annulus is capped and set up for venting to atmosphere via a 1" pipe to surface and a Sentry valve (Sentry replaced with bull plug for testing). Both wells remained in production through the SPBUT period. All annuli of each well have been shut in for testing. The (20"x13") annulus was shut in for 72hrs., the (13"x9") annuli were shut in for 48hrs. and the (9"x5") annuli were shut in for 24hrs. resulting in SPBUTs. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. (John Pazzaglia) and Creston Consultant Reps. (Jason Rajan and Tiffany Smith). Starting at approx. 10:00 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter (cal. 8/11/22). Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for both of the Evelyn Wyo. wells on this pad: - Evelyn Wyo 4H: - (20x13): open casing top in cellar, no bubbling noted * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 0 psi.; 10% gas; Sample taken @ 10:05 - (9x5): 361 psi.; 100% gas; Sample taken @ 10:10 - Evelyn Wyo. 2H: - (20x13): 0 psi.; 0% gas; No sample taken * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 2.2 psi.; 88% gas; Sample taken @ 10:21 - (9x5); 127 psi.; 96% gas; Sample taken @ 10:27 - All annuli were returned to venting by 10:30

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 5/11/2023 to STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC in Howe Twp, Forest county. OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 5/11/2023
Violation Code: OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
Violation ID: 995086
Permit API: 053-29526
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with rods and tubing. The pump jack has been removed from the well, the annulus of the well remains connected to a gathering line. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. The well is not equipped with a well tag, nor is there a site ID sign posted at the location.A tank battery containing four steel tanks and two poly tanks inside of an earthen containment is located approximately 200 feet east of this well. There are indications that production fluids (primarily brine) have repeatedly been released onto the gravel inside of this containment. The soil is stained and specific conductance of the soil is elevated at the western edge where fluid from the tanks appears to have been released, and at the eastern edge of the containment where fluids appear to have been released from a pipeline riser/blow off).Vegetation is absent and deer tracks are very dense on the surface outside of the west/northwest extent of the containment, as it appears the released fluids have migrated through the earthen walls at the natural contour onto which the gravel and earthen wells were constructed. Stained soil and elevated specific conductance continue westward into a roadside ditch of Forest Road 219 until the ditch reaches a cross culvert approximately 300 feet away.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29931, 053-29930, 053-29944, 053-29955 and 053-29945 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. These E and S concerns are considered part of E and S violations that are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29816 (Warrant 2980 #45).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/23/2025 to LPR ENERGY LLC in Snow Shoe Township, Centre county. 78a86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery.  Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: LPR ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/23/2025
Violation Code: 78a86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 8231174
Permit API: 027-21672
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre
Municipality: Snow Shoe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/23/2025
Comments: The weather is 74 Deg. F, sunny at time of inspection of LPR Energy LLC. in conjunction to the Application for Inactive Well Status, Snow Shoe Pad, well # 4-8HG on April 23, 2025. This well is topholed only. Open Hole is drilled to 8,913 ft, 9 5/8" Intermediate casing is set at 2,027 ft., 13 3/8" Surface casing is set at 730’, and Conductor is set at 200’. Intermediate casing pressure is 0 PSI. Proposed horizontal lateral has not been drilled. No production equipment in site. There is one inactive and shut in well on this pad. Annulus (13-3/8 X 9-5/8) is open 100% LEL and 3% combustible gas was detected at the annulus vent; and 0% combustible gas was detected in the cellar area. The Department’s investigation of the above-referenced gas well detected the presence of combustible gas at the 13 3/8" Surface X 9 5/8" Intermediate casing annulus vent. This is a violation of the Department’s regulations relating to Defective Cement, 25 Pa. Code ¿¿78a.86, which provides: "In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under ¿¿ 78.91 – 78.98 (related to plugging)." Please provide a written response detailing how LPR Energy LLC. intends to comply with this regulation, including information regarding the suspected source of stray gas, by 5/23/2025. No LPR Energy LLC. Representatives present DEP Representative - Justin Galioto, Oil and Gas Inspector

Comments: *** This report is to amend inspection (#2931748) performed on 9/11/19. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/25/2024 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Fallowfield Township, Washington county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/25/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8202510
Permit API: 125-23123
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/25/2024
Comments: Inspection 1 of 2:On 09/25/2024, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the POCKY F24 OG Well in Fallowfield Township, Washington County.The following was observed during inspection:-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo 1).-The well and operator's information was displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo 2)-Some corrosion and appeared leaks were observed on the well head and production tank. Some corrosion was observed on production equipment (Photos 3-5). -I observed brown and shiny colored fluid built up near the well head base and surrounding well head fittings. I received elevated readings of 5.74 mS/cm in the base and 5.39 mS/cm around fittings (Photo 6-10).-It appears the fluid has reached the gravel below. I received elevated conductivity readings of 2.23 mS/cm near the base of the well and 8.67 mS/cm, 8.71 mS/cm and 10.32 mS/cm surrounding the well head.-I observed an open threaded valve that is not plugged and there is appeared elevated fluids leaking from the head. Elevated readings of 9.25 mS/cm (Photo 15 and 16).-3.8 pS/cm on metal on well head components (Photo 17).-I observed tubing coming from production tanks laying on the berm and in yellow container. No elevated readings were found in fluid of the container (Photo 21).-Multiple readings were taken surrounding the berm near the tubing and below. Elevated readings of 5.84, 6.11, 3.67, 8.92, 9.00, and 8.32 mS/cm were found on the inside edges of the earth berm near and below the tubing (Photo 18-24).Diversified submitted an order response on August 31st, 2023 of production tank maintenance or removal. Pocky F24 listed as the following: "Last visit date was 08/10/2023 and Tank(s) on location are secure with no visual evidence of a release. Needs attention: NO." properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SLT PRODUCTION LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/02/2023
Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 8154391
Permit API: 123-44951
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/02/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. 3% Methane was detected in slam bar hole #3 utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X Meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023, a viable methane sample was not attainable at the time of inspection. At this time the following violations are being issued against this well. VIOLATION: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING – DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. VIOLATION:78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times At this time the department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to Rockdale Marcellus Llc in Union Twp, Tioga County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-09-03 to Rockdale Marcellus Llc in Union Twp, Tioga county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-03
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 860692
Permit API: 117-22060
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Union Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-09-03
Comments: Results from sample IDs 0718-101, 0718-102, and 0718-103, collected 8/19/2019 as documented in inspection report number 2922630, were received from the laboratory on 8/31/2019. At the time of inspection, a large volume of fluid was observed in the northeast corner of the pad surface and was discharging into the rock-lined stormwater channel, which begins at this corner of the pad, and flowing into the northeast infiltration basin. Conductivity of the fluid on the pad surface in the northeast corner of the pad had electrical conductivity (EC) readings between 4.61 mS/cm and 7.19 mS/cm. In the basin, the fluid entering from the channel had an EC of 5.85 mS/cm. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in samples 0718-101 and 0718-102, collected from the pad surface and the northeast infiltration basin, respectively, indicate that a discharge of a pollutional substance occurred. The discharge of a pollutional substance to the infiltration basin, considered Waters of the Commonwealth, is a violation of Section 401 of the Clean Streams Law. The volume of the release is underdetermined. The Department recommends following the process outlined in 78a66 in order to remediate the release. Violations noted. The violation cited on 8/26/2019 (IR #2925622) remains outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.

Permit API: 115-22551
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp

Comments: Arrived on location at 10:30 to conclude 72hr PBUTs. I was accompanied by Ken Kennedy (OGI supervisor), Eric Rooney (Department Geologist) and Eric Miller ((OGI). We met with Cabot O&G Reps., Ben Whitaker and Keenan Small; Selman and Assoc. Reps., Brett Wambold, Miriah Palmatier and Russell Moult. At ~ 10:25 ending pressures were checked using Cabots digital gauge. Annuli gas checks were performed starting at ~ 12:00 with a MSA Altair 5X multi gas detector that was calibrated on 4/19/21. Following conclusion of area residents domestic well water sampling, all wells annuli were reconnected and flowing through the ALICAT annular flow monitoring set-up. Although gas samples were collected at the cemented annuli of the 2H, 6H, 8H, 12H and 14H wells, there was no flow or pressures noted and no additional violations cited. Left site at 14:40.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to RICE DRILLING B LLC in Wayne Township, Greene County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/26/2023 to RICE DRILLING B LLC in Wayne Township, Greene county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RICE DRILLING B LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/26/2023
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8153915
Permit API: 059-27988
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Wayne Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/26/2023
Comments: On 07/26/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Dahn-Tahn Well Site following an incident report received by the Department on 07/25/2023 (CTS 373808).On 07/25/2023, EQT submitted an incident report after approximately 25 gallons of glycol were released from a dehydrator unit on the pad. Pressure testing occurred, resulting with glycol misting onto pad in an area approximately 25 feet by 25 feet. Spill area approximately 50 feet by 20 feet and 4 inches in depth. The glycol was off containment but contained to the pad. SPSI remediated the impacted area that evening. No obtainable electro conductivity or PID readings. The area appeared remediated upon my arrival. SPSI representative Cody Tokarski onsite 07/25/2023.The following was observed:Container onsite marked, noting remediated, impacted material inside for testing (Photos 1, 2).Impacted area appeared remediated (Photos 3-10).Origin of glycol release (Photo 11).Violations of 91.34(A), 78a57(a), 78a.54, and SWMA 301 are being noted and were immediately corrected. No further violations are being issued at this time.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Sheshequin Twp, Bradford County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/15/2021 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Sheshequin Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/14/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 929653
Permit API: 015-21152
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Sheshequin Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/15/2021
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Chesapeake's Covington well site located in Sheshequin Township, Bradford County on 9/14/2021 at 1340 hours. The weather was 78 degrees with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced water reported to the DEP by Chesapeake. Numerous Chesapeake representatives were on location when I arrived. Chesapeake representatives explained that a connection on the dump line of the GPU onsite had failed, causing the release of produced water into the containment skid of the GPU and then onto the pad surface. Fluid held in the containment skid of the GPU was field measured at Over Ranged (>19.99mS/cm)(photo #2). Damp areas on the both sides of the GPU (photos #3 & 4) were observed and the pad material was determined to be elevated for electrical conductivity and field measured at >4.00mS/cm. The release appears to have migrated towards the area located behind the GPU fenced-in area (photo #7). Soil screenings in this area were also elevated (>4.00mS/cm). A small puddle of water had collected against the earthen containment berm of the pad, behind the GPU (photo #10) and was field measured at Over Range (>19.99mS/cm). The area of impact was roughly estimated at 50 feet x 40 feet. Chesapeake planned to dispatch Creston Environmental to conduct screening and sampling. A plan to remove the GPU in order to begin excavation was put in place. Violations of the following are cited against API #015-21152 at this time: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 I departed the site at 1420 hours.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Fallowfield Township, Washington County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/16/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Fallowfield Township, Washington county. 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/16/2023
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8162888
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/16/2023
Comments: On 10/16/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 10/12/2023 (IR 3630018, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Paul Stiner of Diversified. On 10/12/2023, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued as outstanding for the observed elevated conductivity and the access road condition. The following was observed during inspection on 10/16/2023:The operator had removed impacted soils within the bottom portion of the berm, adjacent to the valve of tank 4. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 1-6). The operator had placed the impacted soils within buckets that were dated (Photos 7, 8).Some soils were removed from the berm adjacent to tank 5. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 9, 10).Regarding the area behind tank 5, it appeared as though the area I initially discovered to have elevated readings, and the operator was not able to replicate my readings, displayed adequate readings on 10/16/23, most likely due to dilution from rain (Photos 11, 12). There was one reading of 3.29 m/S, however this area was small, approximately a 4 inch by 4 inch section (Photo 13). The operator is going to remove some soils from this area, which was marked with a brick (Photo 14). Due to the size of this area, no violation is being noted.The operator explained that the cause of the impacted berm was due to fluids reaching the ground during tank clean out (Photos 15, 16). It is highly recommended to place containment/grate to collect any residual fluids and prevent them from reaching the ground and berm during tank clean out.The access road appeared to remain in poor condition (Photos 17, 18). On 10/13/2023, I had emailed Daniel Frick of Diversified regarding the start time of repairs; Diversified is waiting on bids and can hopefully update me next week (from 10/13 email). As of 10/16/2023, there has not been an update. Also in this email, I had asked if the NOV response for IR 3620008, mentioning the removal of a 5 gallon bucket, was referring to the area under the valve of tank 4 instead of behind tank 5, which was then confirmed to be correct - the material was removed from under the valve. Due to the operator's effort to remediate the impacted areas and the impacted areas appearing in relatively good condition, the violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, and SWMA 301, regarding the release of production fluid, are being closed. Violations of 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a), regarding the access road, remain outstanding.
