properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/29/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/29/2025
Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 8242708
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2025
Comments: On July 29, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQTs Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 7/28/2025 at 2:54 pm.The spill report stated that at 2:06 pm on 7/28/2025, over 5 gallons of production fluids were found on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site after removing secondary containment. Accompanying during today's inspection is EQTs representative Kyle Borden.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had different Operator information on it than the Act 9 sign. The DEP recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. At the time of this inspection, drill outs were recently completed on the 6U and containment was removed from the well pad the day prior. Mr. Borden stated that the secondary containment in the release area was packed with tanks and large equipment, therefore despite routine inspections of the containment, only the edges of the containment could be inspected, and no holes or tears were observed. However, upon removal of the containment, staining and small puddles were observed on the gravel pad in an approximately 115 ft x 60 ft area. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to wellheads covered by boxes. The pea gravel in this area was observed to be wet with sections that appeared to be darker in color than other areas. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI and Moody were arriving on site to remediate the release and that they estimate remediation to be completed within the day. EQT representative Schuyler Brounce mentioned in his email (documented in IR 4024285), that following his review of the incident, he estimates the release to be over 1 barrel. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Borden stated once all contaminated gravel has been removed, an updated quantity will be provided to the DEP.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected soil readings of 1.835 mS, 3.22 mS, 3.35 mS and 2.08 mS in the incident area closest to the wellheads, as well as 2.56 mS between two wellheads and a fluid reading of Over Range in fluid observed to be pooled in secondary containment adjacent to the release area. These conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil reading of 0.1457 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign.At the time of this inspection, the DEP requested secondary containment logs for the Porter well pad and Mr. Borden stated they would be provided to the Department electronically. The DEP is also requesting an electronic copy of the Safety Data Sheets for all chemicals stored/utilized within and near the secondary containment that was observed to have the release underneath by COB 8/5/2025.The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the over 1 barrel release of production fluids on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

Comments: Follow up inspection of the Yahner 1 well conducted on 10/27/2022. Arrived on location at 9:40. Violations were issued during a 3/23/2021 inspection (Inspection Record No. 3166383) for: OGA3211(H) - Failure to install permit number on well. 78.88(A) - Failure to record and retain MIA inspection results. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for MIA inspections. 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it. A follow up inspection was conducted on 3/10/2022 (Inspection Record No. 3327521). This inspection found that none of the previously cited violations had been addressed or responded to and all violations remained outstanding. This 10/26/2022 follow up inspection found that the well remains in a similar condition/configuration as the previous inspections. Well head and tie in line is the only equipment installed. No additional production equipment on location. Appears to have been a new line installed to the well as seen by the adjacent earth disturbance at the time of inspection. There is no API or other identification posted on location. Review found that no Annual Production Reports or Mechanical Integrity Assessment Reports have been submitted. Well is still reported as Inactive Status although the Inactive Status expired on 1/1/2018. Due to failing to return the well to Active status, a violation of 78.104 is issued - terms of Inactive Status. Due to no production of the well reported it is considered abandoned. All previously issued violations remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/02/2026 to EQT ARO LLC in Cascade Township, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2026
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8276365
Permit API: 081-20961
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/02/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 6/1/26 a release of an unknown volume of brine-contaminated stormwater occurred outside of containment. The notification also stated that Tobias was dispatched on the morning of 6/2/26 to conduct excavation of impacted pad material. A wireline operator was working on the 5H well when I arrived on location. An aboveground storage tank (AST) is present on the pad along with a gas buster tank. Well site secondary containment consisting of a secondary containment liner, containment berms, and rig mats is present around the well heads. Fluid was present on the containment. Fluid was observed on the pad surface on the north side and on the south side of the containment. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid on the north side of the containment ranged from 1 mS/cm to 2.27 mS/cm. On the south side of the containment the soil is damp but no ponded fluid was observed. The soil EC probe gave a reading of 1.07 mS/cm where the soil was the most damp. On the containment, the EC of the fluid ranged from 700 uS/cm to 3.25 mS/cm. The rest of the well pad and surrounding area appeared very dry.During this inspection, crews were working to remove the fluid from the containment, remove rig mats from the containment, and identify holes in the containment liner. Tobias was also onsite with excavation equipment and a roll-off box. Before I left the location, Tobias began to excavate the impacted pad material and place it into the roll-off box.I met with EQT representative Zac Subra during this inspection. He said that the well site secondary containment had been installed on 5/11/26 for upcoming refrac operations on the 5H well. He also said that the AST was for freshwater to be used for hydrostatic testing of the well. He said that a workover rig has prepped the 5H well for the upcoming refrac and there had been tanks containing produced fluid on the pad at that time. He said that some volume of produced fluid must have been released to the containment. He relayed that crews had so far found 3 holes in the secondary containment liner. He said that the gas buster tank on the pad was empty.I took sample 0718-273 from the pad surface north of the well site secondary containment. I took sample 0718-274 from the fluid on the well site secondary containment.On the same day at 1203, I spoke with Rick Hall of EQT. He stated that on the morning of 6/1/26, the fluid on the pad surface was initially observed and the EC was 1 mS/cm. He said the fluid was checked again throughout the day and the EC climbed until it reached 3.2 mS/cm by the evening. He said they took a sample of the fluid at that time. He said the notification to the Department was made the following morning. I recommended to him that EQT pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown release volume and he said they would. Violations noted.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Point View Road in March 2006. Since the most recent inspection of the site on 8/30/2021 (Inspection Record # 3242810), work has been started on remediation of the site. A spill was reported to the Department on 11:03 AM on August 27, 2021. The spill occurred from a broken copper line attached to the wellhead. The estimated volume lost from this spill was 2 bbl. During this inspection, it was noted that the production equipment has been disconnected and staged along the edge of the restored site. Stressed vegetation and contaminated soil has been removed from the site. A response to the NOV has been received by the Department. The response states that five tri-axle loads of contaminated soil and vegetation were removed from the site. The response also states that the excavation will be left open until the attainment of standards from the Alternative Remediation Process has been demonstrated. The violations at the site can be closed when the contaminated soil has been replaced, the site has been graded to final contours, and the manifest and tipping information for soil disposal has been received by the Department.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to NUCOMER ENERGY LLC in Hickory Twp, Forest County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/12/2022 to NUCOMER ENERGY LLC in Hickory Twp, Forest county. OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: NUCOMER ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/12/2022
Violation Code: OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
Violation ID: 978529
Permit API: 053-30164
Unconventional: Yes
County: Forest
Municipality: Hickory Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2022
Comments: On 12/12/2022, I conducted a follow up inspection of the DR02 Pad and Impoundment ESX 1H well. Nucomer has hired a 3rd party contractor "Assist" to complete the secondary containment liner repair. TJ Pennino from EMKEY Gathering was on site representing Nucomer Energy. This is in response to violations in previous inspections(3459581). The violations are for tears and holes in the secondary containment liner in the tank battery. Two different methods were being utilized in the repair attempt. One is a hot air weld of liner material. The second was a PVC extruder gun as seen in photo #3. It should be noted the original containment liner is thickness of 20 mil. The patch material brought by Assist for the hot air welding is a 40 mil thickness. After several attempts to hot air weld the patch material to the existing liner, it was evident trying to weld the 40 mil patch material to the 20 mil existing material was not going to work. Several pieces of the 20 mil liner were cut from outside containment and cleaned as best as possible. Again the original liner material is too thin and was not supporting a good hot-air weld. The extruder was used on several smaller holes. It became obvious it is not suitable to be used on a material of this thickness. The temperature was set as low as the machine would allow and the material melted through the original liner (pictures #1 and #4).After several attempts trying several different methods, the decision was made by TJ to abandon the repair attempt. TJ was going to speak with ASSIST and plan another course of action and discuss options available.Additionally the violation for the 55 gallon drums being stored outside of secondary containment, can be closed. This violation has been resolved.

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8244480
Permit API: 081-22038
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/07/2025
Comments: On August 7, 2025, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection to a reported spill at the Expand Energy Elly May Well Pad. On August 6, 2025 at 1638, Expand Energy reported to the spill hotline that fluid with elevated conductivity was found outside of the containment on the well pad surface. Expand Energy estimated that approximately 32 gallons was leaked outside of the containment. Upon arrival at the well pad, Expand was vacuuming out the suspected containment causing the leak to the well pad. DEP screened the conductivity of the free liquid that had pooled next to the secondary containment and resulted in 2,570 uS/cm. The area where the free liquid had pooled next to the secondary containment was about 25 feet by 15 feet. After the containment was completely emptied and moved to determine the extent of the leak, a small hole was found in the plastic liner of the containment. Expand then vacuumed up the free liquid on the well pad surface. Mike Deming with Expand Energy arrived shortly after the free liquid had been vacuumed from the well pad surface. Mr. Deming explained that Expand had recently washed down the timber mats in this secondary containment. So the water leaking from containment was a mixture of wash down water and rainwater. Mr. Deming said that Expand expects to have a piece of machinery at the well pad by noon to begin excavating the contaminated soil in the area of impact. Mr. Deming said that Creston Environmental was scheduled to delineate the spill and confirm the remediation of the spill. DEP left the site prior to Expand beginning the excavation of the area of impact. At 1445, Mr. Deming called DEP to report the area of impact had been excavated. In an email provided by Mr. Deming, the area of excavation was approximately 19' by 29' with an average depth of 4". The conductivity of the soil after scraping the contaminated soil from the area of impact was less than 450 uS/cm. Mr. Deming said approximately 8.75 tons of contaminated soil was placed in a lined dumpster. Based on the amount of contaminated soil removed and the calculation completed for the amount of liquid that soil could hold, 32 gallons is the volume leaked from containment onto the well pad surface. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 have been noted. Due to the immediate remediation of the spill the violations are considered corrected.

Inactive status.(a) General rule.--Upon application, the department shall grant inactive status for a period of five years for a permitted or registered well, if the following requirements are met:(1) the condition of the well is sufficient to prevent damage to the producing zone or contamination of fresh water or other natural resources or surface leakage of any substance;(2) the condition of the well is sufficient to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore and is adequate to protect freshwater aquifers, unless the department determines the well poses a threat to the health and safety of persons or property or to the environment;

The results of the gas screenings and flow checks for each well are listed below: - 5H - (20x13) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 3,420 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 900 ppm gas initially, 640 ppm gas peak and 320 ppm gas sustained (9x5) annulus: 18.6 Cu/ft per day; 90% gas initially, 73% gas peak and 73% gas sustained - 6H - (20x13) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 0 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 200 ppm gas initially, 400 ppm gas peak and 400 ppm gas sustained (9x5) annulus: 16.0 Cu/ft per day; 95% gas initially, 95% gas peak and 95% gas sustained - 21HC - (20x13) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 0 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 1,520 ppm gas initially, 600 ppm gas peak and 300 ppm gas sustained (9x5) annulus: 2.3 Cu/ft per day; 60% gas initially, 15% gas peak and 15% gas sustained - 22HC - (20x13) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 80 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 1,800 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained (9x5) annulus: 65.3 Cu/ft per day; 85% gas initially, 61% gas peak and 50% gas sustained - 23HC - (20x13) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 260 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day (no balloon inflation); 1,040 ppm gas initially, 260 ppm gas peak and 260 ppm gas sustained (9x5) annulus: 65.4 Cu/ft per day; 73% gas initially, 65% gas peak and 65% gas sustained All annuli were shut in today at 10:00 on the (5) wells to be tested. Pressure and gas screenings will be performed on Thurs. (10/24/24) resulting in a 72 hr. PBUTs for each well.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/16/2026 to HOWARD DRILLING INC in Wetmore Township, McKean county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: HOWARD DRILLING INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/16/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8281856
Permit API: 083-57684
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/16/2026
Comments: I conducted a routine inspection of this recently completed well. A moderate amount of water was present in the ditch line next to the well, without significant rain in the past several days I checked the conductivity of the fluid and soil in the ditch line, readings from 4280 S to over 18000 S were present.Looking closer at the area of the partially reclaimed pit, a group of trees appeared to be stressed and dropping their leaves. On the eastern side of the pit readings between 4000 and 15000 S were observed in several locations.An unknown amount of brine/frac fluid has been released, its extent is currently unknown at this time but it seems to be less than one barrel and appears to have stayed close to the edge of the pit. Future inspections will be done to assess if the spill was more significant and has traveled further than initially observed and to evaluate the cleanup of the documented release.Please email confirmation of this inspection to ebruce@pa.gov

Violation Code: 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.

Permit API: 125-28726
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/05/2024
Comments: On 08/05/2024, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the REDD Well Pad in Fallowfield Township, Washington County.The following was observed during inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo 1).-The Emergency Response Plan was on site.- Well site entrance and access road appeared to be constructed and maintained (Photo 2).- PCSM Basin appeared to be constructed and functioning properly (Photo 4 and 5).-I observed a plugging access road was constructed along the well pad slope and between the PSCM basin (Photo 7-9).A slope failure 90 x 5 feet wide and was found by the department on the well pad slope. Site status is production. There is no significant threat to the well pad. Waters of the Commonwealth is not affected. It appears that temporary stabilization was installed (Photo 9-12).- Overall, the well pad slope appeared to be constructed and vegetated properly. Well plugging is located and constructed along the well pad slope (Photo 13-17).- Production fluid tanks and GPU appeared to be in sound condition. GPUs are in secondary containment (Photo 19-21).-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo 22).-Fresh water impoundment was constructed and functioning properly and slopes are vegetated (Photo 23-25).The department request date of when the slope failure was reported. Violations were issued for: 102.5(m)4, 102.11(a)1, 78a53, 102.4(b)1, 102.22(a).

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/07/2025 to DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/07/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8233007
Permit API: 129-26521
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2025
Comments: On May 7, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3967072 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3967072, it appeared that excavation and remediation work had started onsite as a covered excavation stockpile was observed at the well site.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5). The covered excavation stockpile that was observed onsite during the time IR 3967072 remains, in addition to another covered excavation stockpile at the downslope end of the impacted area. They appear to be from remediation work that has been conducted thus far (see photos 6, 9, and 11). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank during the time of IR 3965337 remains covered with plastic sheeting, and appears to have been excavated near the brine tank and the downslope end of the impacted area (see photos 7, 8, and 10). Oil absorbent booms remain placed downslope of the covered impacted area (see photo 12). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected downslope of impacted area (see photos 14 and 15).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remediation work remains ongoing and the impacted area remains adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.
